products.name: JJNSOLAR 200W N-type Bifacial Solar Panel (single panel)
specs: 200 W per panel; sold in packs of 1 to 10 panels (up to 2,000 W)
N-type, triple-cut, bifacial (rear side also collects light)
12 V, 24 V and 48 V batteries and solar generators (per listing)
Rigid tempered glass, aluminum frame, IP68 junction box
182 W measured of 200 W rated (OutdoorGearLab, earlier JJN bifacial 200W, two hours of clear sun)
products.warranty: 30-year performance warranty per the JJN listing. The listing doesn't state a product (workmanship) warranty term. Reviewers have quoted 18 months and 5 years, so confirm it with JJN before you order.
products.returns: We couldn't read JJN's return policy on 2026-11-14 because the store was rate-limiting requests. Inspect and test the panel on delivery, and report any damage right away.
products.summary: A rigid 200 W bifacial glass panel at about 75 cents a rated watt. JJN's earlier bifacial 200W made 182 W of 200 W in OutdoorGearLab's 12-panel test, the highest share of any panel tested.
products.fit: Best for a permanent mount: RV or van roof, roof rack, shed, or a ground stand where light can also reach the back. Not for carrying to a campsite.
caveats: OutdoorGearLab's 182 W result is for JJN's earlier bifacial 200W. We found no independent test of the N-type version sold now.
Rigid glass panel, about 25 lb. It needs brackets or a rack.
Buyers report panels from JJN and other brands arriving with cracked glass. Open the box and test the panel the day it arrives.
The MC4 leads are short and OutdoorGearLab found them hard to unplug. Plan on an MC4 extension cable.
Measure the space between your roof vents first. The tested panel is about 54 × 30 in.

products.name: JJNSOLAR 425W N-type Bifacial Solar Panel (Updated Packaging)
specs: Anodized aluminum frame, thicker tempered glass, IP68
products.warranty: 30-year performance warranty per the JJN listing. The listing doesn't state a product (workmanship) warranty term, so confirm it with JJN.
products.returns: We couldn't read JJN's return policy on 2026-11-14 because the store was rate-limiting requests. Inspect the panels on delivery.
products.summary: A large 425 W bifacial panel for shed, cabin and ground arrays. Four panels (1,700 W) cost $1,144, about 67 cents a watt.
products.fit: Best for ground mounts and fixed arrays feeding an MPPT charge controller or a power station with a high-voltage solar input.
caveats: This is a high-voltage residential-size panel. It needs an MPPT controller, not a small 12 V PWM controller. Check the label's open-circuit voltage against your controller's limit.
Big and heavy for one person to lift onto a roof. We couldn't verify the weight.
JJN also has an older listing of this panel (original packaging) from $295. We couldn't read its pack prices.

codes.terms: The Awin listing we were given doesn't state the discount or what it applies to. Not cart-tested.

notes: QUERY: 'best 200 watt solar panel'. Google autocomplete today suggested it along with 'for rv', 'for camping', 'for the money' and 'reddit'. The pages answering it today are thin: undated affiliate roundups (thewearify, solarreviews 'in 2024', foliumbiosciences) built from listing specs. OutdoorGearLab's 12-panel test is the only measured comparison. PAIN POINTS (10 sources): output below the rating 6 (OGL table, two Van Living Forum threads, Renogy owner review via search, RV Outfitting, ShopSavvy); glass broken on arrival 5 (ShopSavvy 'numerous' for Renogy, Sienna Solar JJN 1 of 6, another JJN buyer 2 of 3 orders, desertcart JJN 'shattered' with good support, RV Outfitting); short or awkward MC4 leads 3; controller or voltage mismatch 3 (ShopSavvy '12V listed but 23V', solar-electric forum, GoodSam); roof fit around vents 2; failures around 10-12 months or slow warranty handling 1 (RV Outfitting). SEGMENTS AND WINNERS: (1) fixed mount on RV, van or shed, best value: JJN 200W bifacial. Its earlier version measured 182/200 W (91%), the best ratio of the 12 panels, with OGL's lowest cost per measured watt. It sells for $149 per panel vs BougeRV's rigid 16BB bifacial from $188.99. (2) folding panel for a power station: Renogy 200W Portable (177 W, 14.8 lb, OGL Editors' Choice). It is sold on Renogy and Amazon, not an approved program, so it gets a named row with a maker URL and no buy link. EcoFlow NextGen 220W made more raw output (193 W) but lists around $649. (3) curved roof: BougeRV Arch 200W flexible (166 W, 6.6 lb, OGL Top Pick), maker URL only. No approved CJ/Awin brand beats Renogy for folding or BougeRV for flexible. NOT VERIFIED: the JJN 200W product endpoint returned HTTP 429 all session (several runs share this IP), so I could not see the per-variant breakdown.
